characteristics: ~2A4-era Abrams standard, not latest M1A2 SEPv3
Strength: Same ammo family as Leopard 2 simplifies logistics; strong frontal armor
Limitation: Gas turbine is fuel-hungry and maintenance-intensive; the variant sent is an older M1A1 standard, not the newest US configuration
employment_notes: 31 delivered (2023); used sparingly and reportedly withdrawn from frontline use at points due to drone vulnerability — illustrates the broader 'any MBT is a target' finding rather than being Abrams-specific
contrast_vs_traditional: Abrams doctrine assumed a resupply chain moving fuel and ammunition behind the front under a friendly air umbrella — a fair assumption for a gas-turbine tank that burns through fuel fast. Persistent drone ISR turns that same resupply route into the most-watched terrain in the sector, so keeping an Abrams fighting now depends on a logistics tail that can dodge exactly the kind of standoff observation the tank itself was never built to out-drive.
